identity.title: ALMA Observations of the T Tauri Binary System AS 205: Evidence for Molecular Winds and/or Binary Interactions

paper_type_evidence.quote: we present high-resolution millimeter observations of the dust and gas disk of the T Tauri star AS 205 N and its companion, AS 205 S, obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array.

evidence.quote: AS 205 is located at the northern edge of the Ophiuchus star forming region, at a distance of $\sim$125 pc (cite: Mamajek08; Loinard08).
AS 205 is located at the northern edge of the Ophiuchus star forming region, at a distance of $\sim$125 pc (cite: Mamajek08; Loinard08).

question.value: Does the gas disk of AS 205 N show non-Keplerian motion and extended emission on ALMA scales, and is it due to disk winds, binary tidal interaction, or other causes?

evidence.quote: also displays significant deviations from Keplerian disk emission in the observations presented here.
Two possible explanations for these observations hold up best to close scrutiny — tidal interaction with AS 205 S or disk winds (or a combination of the two)
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00531.S.
Detections near both AS 205 N and S are obtained in 1.3$\,$mm continuum

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Four 117 MHz spectral windows, 30.5 kHz channels (0.04 km/s), resolution 61 kHz (0.08 km/s); windows at 13CO, 12CO, C18O and CH3OH (continuum)

evidence.quote: Observations were obtained in four spectral windows of width 117 MHz, with a channel width of 30.5 kHz (0.04 km s$^{-1}$)
Fifteen 12-meter antennas were available for both sets of observations
with the Cycle 0 extended configuration
On 27 Mar, the minimum and maximum baselines were 43 and 402 meters
the synthesized beam is approximately $\sim 0.7'' \times 0.5''$ with a position angle of $\sim 90^\circ-100^\circ$ degrees
with a maximum spatial scale of $\sim8'' = 1000$ AU
The total on-source integration time for each set of observations was 15.8 minutes, for a total integration time of 31.6 minutes.
Observations of AS 205 N and S were obtained on UT 27 Mar 2012 and 04 May 2012

analysis_steps.goal: Build disk models and simulate ALMA observations

method.value: RADMC dust and RADLite line radiative transfer; simobserve/simanalyze; compare to channel and moment maps

analysis_steps.goal: Test origin scenarios and wind model

method.value: Compare observations with cloud, envelope, circumbinary, tidal and RADLite wind models; estimate mass-loss rate

evidence.quote: We find that the nominal wind model does not produce any appreciable extended emission, beyond that expected for a disk

the separation of the two disks is $1.3''$, and the position angle of the binary is 214$^\circ$

findings_qualitative.value: 12CO emission extends to ~2'' from AS 205 N with non-axisymmetric excess to the northeast and an S-shaped non-Keplerian velocity field deviating by ~1 km/s

evidence.quote: The observations deviate from expectation by as much as $\sim$1 km s$^{-1}$.

findings_qualitative.value: Cloud emission, envelope and circumbinary accretion are disfavored

evidence.quote: we believe it’s unlikely that we are observing accretion streams from a circumbinary disk

claims.hypothesis: Is the gas around AS 205 N purely Keplerian?
claims.experiment: Compare 12CO and 13CO moment maps with a disk model
claims.result: Extended asymmetric emission and ~1 km/s velocity deviations
claims.finding: AS 205 N is not solely a Keplerian disk

evidence.quote: It is clear from these observations that AS 205 N does not solely consist of a Keplerian gas disk

claims.hypothesis: Is extended emission from a circumbinary disk accretion stream?
claims.experiment: Derive CO mass upper limit for a ring at 2''-6'' and compare to GG Tau and UY Aur

evidence.quote: we derive an upper limit to the mass of a circumbinary disk around AS 205 of $10^{-4}\,M_\odot$

claims.hypothesis: Can a disk wind or tidal stripping explain the features?
claims.experiment: Compare with RADLite wind models and tidal resonance arguments
claims.result: Wind models give a curved velocity field but no extended emission unless modified; tidal resonance problematic
claims.finding: Neither fully explains; a combination remains possible

evidence.quote: no single scenario is able to completely explain these features.

why_this_data.value: Low-J 12CO 2-1 may trace wind on larger scales; target had IR evidence for a disk wind

evidence.quote: a low-critical-density, low-excitation tracer like $^{12}$CO $J=2-1$ may be a good choice for detecting a wind on larger scales

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Molecular cloud emission, envelope remnant, circumbinary accretion, and flyby encounters considered and disfavored

evidence.quote: Therefore, we do not believe that molecular cloud emission can be the cause of the observed spatially extended emission.

limitations_admitted.value: Model degeneracies; fluxes scaled by hand; mass of AS 205 S uncertain

evidence.quote: Since our limited information would result in strong model degeneracies were we to try to exactly match the observed data

referee_caveats_inferred: Models compared by eye with no quantitative fit
Residuals depend on disk model scaling
Mass estimates depend on assumed excitation temperature

missing_for_reproduction: Imaging parameters such as cell and image size
